title: Alphabet loses $500B in a day — its own AI Mode is eating search ads
summary: Alphabet has its worst day ever as search ads slow, partly because of Google's own AI Mode, while its free cash flow goes negative under a $205 billion buildout; the selloff spreads to chips and Intel. Then CSET's step-by-step map of black-box distillation and the number nobody can see, and Nathan Lambert grading his own prediction that open-weight models were fine for cyber.

topics: Alphabet's record one-day drop (Oct 29, 2026): -12.6%, ~$500B, second-largest wipeout after Nvidia's $589B (Jan 2025); search ads (~half of revenue) grew 12%, slowest in five quarters, partly from AI Mode producing fewer ads; Q3 capex $51.4B, free cash flow -$9.1B (second negative quarter), up to $205B capex this year, >$1T multiyear commitments; Friday spread: Nasdaq 100 -3.4% intraday, SOX -7.2%, Intel -29% on memory crunch; Amazon trailing FCF -$42.4B, $220B capex; Microsoft FCF +$18.6B, capex $45.2B under $50B plan on third-party capacity delays; $326B big-tech debt in 2026 (S&P GMI); Epoch: AI chip compute sold per quarter ~2.5x/yr, 9.1-month doubling

CSET's black-box distillation explainer (Miller, Shea-Blymyer, 26 Oct 2026): white-box vs black-box; five steps (objective, seeds, steering, generation at scale, student training via SFT or feedback/RL/on-policy); adversarial students are huge (R1 >670B) so the goal is post-training, not compression; Anthropic per-lab counts (Alibaba 151M, Moonshot 23M, DeepSeek 12.1M exchanges); outside 150-400B-token estimate = 14-36% of GLM-4.5 post-training data, 30-80% of synthetic reasoning tokens if all used; US labs can't see the final step; one Meta employee used 281B tokens; CSET asks labs to disclose token counts and publish uplift research

Nathan Lambert's 'Was I wrong about open models & cyber risks?': after 'Black October' (PHP2Shell, GitLab) he is 'not sure fine is the right word' for an open-weight Mythos, calls it 'a forced industry update', but holds that closed models did much of the recent hacking, defenders adopt open models faster than attackers, open models are expensive to serve; reads strained first responders (WSJ) as the system working; frames cyber as capability and diffusion, not open vs closed; 'I largely still stand by ... but I'm nervous about it'

dives.why_it_matters: Anyone whose budget, job or vendor choice rides on the AI buildout: the first time the cash machine paying for it flickered, and AI Mode was part of why.
Policy and open-model people get the mechanism and the numbers behind pending distillation rules, including the step no US lab can see.
The open-weights side's leading voice revisits its cyber bet in public, days before Kimi K3.1's open weights are due.
